Instruction condition is an unordered factor coded with two planned sum-to-zero contrasts:
= (−1/3, −1/3, 2/3), structure explained (C3) against not explained (C1, C2), and
= (−1/2, 1/2, 0), rules mentioned (C2) against not mentioned (C1). Planned contrasts are reported unadjusted; pairwise comparisons are Holm-adjusted.

Estimates are on the scale of the model (log units, logit, log-odds or degrees, as stated for each model). The coefficient of a condition contrast in a fixed-effects table is the contrast at the value zero of the covariates with which the condition interacts; the planned contrast is computed from the estimated means and can therefore differ from it. p-values below .001 are printed as < .001. In the figures, filled points mark estimates whose 95 % confidence interval excludes zero; this is an unadjusted criterion and does not replace the corrected tests in the tables.
